newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs move listlessly in dull market.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs move listlessly in dull market.

text.p: Japanese short-term interest rate futures made an unexciting start to their new extended trading schedule on SIMEX, with activity confined to a tight three-tick range for most of Tuesday.

SIMEX extended trading hours for Euroyen futures and options by one hour to 1205 GMT with effect from Tuesday to avoid widening the gap between the close of its pit session and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's open as Chicago goes off daylight saving time.
The March Euroyen contract was settled at 99.30 unchanged from the CME close while June was at 99.14 against 99.16 for the CME. Turnover for both months was 9,259 lots.
June became the lead month on TIFFE after its volume exceeded March for two straight days.
Dealers said interest had dwindled in the March contract after it reached a contract high of 99.36 last week, effectively pricing out an interest rate hike before its expiry next year.

"There's been a bit of consolidation on the Euroyen and JGB (Japanese government bond) futures, which is not surprising after day after day of record highs," said a dealer with a European institution.

He said JGB futures also came under pressure as Japanese players sold them to hedge against their cash positions, but he added the December contract would be bought on any dips to 122.80 and 122.60. It ended at 122.90 against an opening 122.96.
Eurodollar futures finished slightly firmer as players awaited the release of the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI), due on Wednesday.
Dealers said the market would look to the CPI for confirmation the economy was not overheating following last Friday's release of a relatively benign Producer Price Index.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.29 against their IMM close at 94.28. June were at 94.16 against 94.13.
